subject: Civil Engineering
title: Rockfall Protection
description: A quick, practical guide to Rockfall Protection.

hook.text: A boulder bouncing down a mountain highway kills drivers without warning.

buildup.text: Rock catch fences are steel nets anchored to the hillside. They absorb boulder impacts.

discovery.text: Ditches at the toe of slopes catch fallen rocks before they reach the road.

twist.text: Draped mesh holds loose rocks in place on the face — preventing detachment entirely.

climax.text: Switzerland uses galleries — concrete tunnels built over roads under dangerous cliffs.

punchline.text: You can't stop rocks from falling, but you can catch them.

quiz.question: How do rock catch fences protect roads from rockfall?
options: They prevent rocks from forming on the cliff face
Steel nets absorb the energy of falling boulders before they reach the road
They redirect fallen rocks back up the slope

details.summary: Rockfall protection systems prevent dislodged rock from reaching roads, railways, and buildings below steep slopes. Active protection stabilizes rock in place using rock bolts, mesh, and shotcrete.
details.whyItMatters: Rockfall kills people and damages infrastructure in mountainous regions worldwide. Protection systems are essential for safe transportation corridors through steep terrain.
takeaways: Rock bolts and mesh stabilize loose blocks on the source slope face
Flexible ring net barriers absorb impact energy from falling rocks up to several tons
Catch ditches at slope base collect smaller rocks before they reach the road

faq.question: How do flexible rockfall barriers stop high-energy rock impacts?
faq.answer: Flexible barriers use ring nets or cable panels suspended between steel posts with energy-absorbing brake elements on the anchor cables. When a rock hits the net, the brake elements deform progressively, absorbing kinetic energy over a longer distance and reducing peak impact force.

faq.question: How is rockfall hazard assessed along transportation corridors?
faq.answer: Assessment combines geological mapping of unstable rock sources, analysis of discontinuity patterns and block sizes, historical rockfall records, climate factors like freeze-thaw cycles and rainfall, and rockfall trajectory simulation.
